parts.note: read plainly, a trench doing the work of a barrier
the setter means the sunken boundary of an English country-house park, invisible from the house

explanation.walkthrough: The name is said to come from the surprised laugh of walkers who nearly fall into the hidden trench.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken trench with a retaining wall keeps livestock out of landscaped gardens without spoiling the view.

parts.note: read plainly, a general description of self-government
the setter means the specific term, famous from the Irish campaigns of the late nineteenth century

explanation.definitionFit: Self-government of a region by its own parliament within a larger state is the standard term for this.

parts.note: read plainly, any relative of the birch
the setter means the small nut-bearing tree classed in the Betulaceae

explanation.definitionFit: The cobnut and filbert tree belongs botanically to the same plant group as birches and alders.

parts.note: read plainly, anyone who disagrees
the setter means one who raises a formal protest, as in a conscientious one

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises a protest or refuses to go along with a proposal is so called.

clue.text: Clearly written down — admitting no middle way

definitions.meaning: first meaning: set out in print, ink on paper, as in 'I have it in ...'
second meaning: seeing everything as one extreme or its opposite, with no shades of grey

explanation.definitionFit: Dark ink on pale paper gives the idiom for written proof, and two stark opposite colours suggest uncompromising judgement.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to omit or slur over a sound in speech
second meaning: to cut short or run parts together

explanation.definitionFit: Dropping a vowel or syllable when speaking, or cutting out passages, both mean leaving something out.

parts.note: read plainly, anything that accompanies a flash in the sky
the setter means the loud rumbling noise of a storm

explanation.definitionFit: The crash and rumble heard during storms follows every electrical discharge through the sky.

parts.note: read plainly, to make a sail smaller
the setter means the sailor's verb for rolling or tying in part of the canvas

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors reduce the area of canvas exposed to strong wind by tying it in at the reef points.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old and dialect name for the spiny animal
second meaning: a scruffy, mischievous street child

explanation.definitionFit: The word first named the prickly creature, then was applied to poor, ragged children roaming the streets.

parts.note: read plainly, any dance from Poland
the setter means the lively triple-time folk dance Chopin wrote many of

explanation.definitionFit: This lively triple-time folk form from the Mazovia region was popularised in concert music by Chopin.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make used to something unpleasant
second meaning: to toughen against hardship

explanation.definitionFit: Repeated exposure to something unpleasant makes a person used to it and less sensitive.

parts.note: read plainly, any male first name
the setter wants a particular five-letter one, found only from the crossing letters

explanation.definitionFit: This is a common masculine given name of Old Norse origin, meaning roughly wolf counsel.

parts.note: read plainly, people cooperating as a crowd
the setter means pressing and folding dough or clay with the hands

explanation.definitionFit: A baker pummels and folds dough with the hands until it becomes smooth and elastic.

parts.note: read plainly, without match
the setter means having no rival of the same rank or standing

explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no rivals of comparable rank or quality stands above all others.

parts.note: read plainly, any way of getting to know more
the setter means the graph-derived phrase for the rate at which skill is acquired

explanation.definitionFit: Psychologists plot skill gained against practice time, and the phrase now names any period of mastering something new.

parts.note: read plainly, to complete a task
the setter means to bring about a goal by effort

explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a goal successfully through effort or skill is a direct synonym of carrying it out.

parts.note: read plainly, any starchy plant of hot countries
the setter means the root crop from which tapioca comes, in a less common spelling

explanation.walkthrough: This is a variant spelling of cassava, also called manioc.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuberous roots of this shrub yield tapioca flour and are a staple food in many warm countries.

parts.note: read plainly, to stay right behind
the setter means to tail someone secretly, as a detective does

explanation.definitionFit: A detective trailing a suspect keeps as close as the dark outline cast by a body in sunlight.

parts.note: read plainly, any city in India
the setter wants a particular five-letter one, home of the national capital

explanation.definitionFit: This large northern metropolis contains New Delhi, seat of the national government of the republic.

definitions.note: the clue has no definition; the whole instruction stands in for it and the crossing letters confirm the instrument

indicators.note: the short form of anagram tells the solver to rearrange the letters of the referenced entry

parts.note: the answer to 20 down, the ankle bones

explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives no definition, only the instruction; the crossing letters pick out the Indian stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearranged letters spell the long-necked plucked lute of Indian classical music, made famous by Ravi Shankar.

parts.note: read plainly, bones near the foot
the setter means the anatomical Latin plural for the group of small bones there

explanation.definitionFit: Anatomists use this Latin plural for the seven small bones joining the leg to the foot.

parts.note: read plainly, any serve that wins a point
the setter means tennis serves the receiver cannot touch at all

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a serve untouched by the opponent scores outright and takes its name from top playing cards.

parts.note: read plainly, any fisherman's container
the setter means the wicker pannier for carrying a catch of fish

explanation.definitionFit: Fishermen carry their catch in this wicker container, often slung over the shoulder by a strap.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turned the other way up
second meaning: working contrary, as in a relation where one thing rises as the other falls

explanation.definitionFit: Something flipped over is in reversed position, and quantities varying contrarily show the mathematical sense.

parts.note: read plainly, a single instance of something
the setter means one sample taken as typical of its kind

explanation.definitionFit: A single sample taken for study or display represents its whole type or class.

parts.note: read plainly, any sign of displeasure
the setter means making the sibilant sound an audience aims at a villain

explanation.definitionFit: Theatre audiences make a long sibilant noise at villains or poor performers to signal displeasure.
